title: Aegean Seafood Orzo Bowl with Roasted Garlic and Fennel
summary: This vibrant Greek noodle bowl brings together classic Mediterranean flavors and fresh seafood in a hearty format. Crisp octopus pieces and succulent wild shrimp are seared with Greek olive oil, then tossed over warm orzo noodles that have absorbed a delicate tomato, lemon, and fennel reduction. Red onion, brine-cured kalamata olives, and crumbled barrel-aged feta cheese add layers of savory contrast throughout the dish. A scattering of fresh dill and toasted pine nuts provides texture, making each forkful bright and satisfying. Prepared using traditional coastal techniques, this noodle bowl celebrates coastal traditions while providing a well-balanced meal suitable for formal gatherings or elevated family suppers. Rich in lean protein, healthy fats, and aromatic herbs, it delivers an authentic taste of the islands directly to your home kitchen without requiring overly complex kitchen equipment.

steps.step: Rinse the octopus tentacle thoroughly under cold running water to remove any surface residual grit.
Place the octopus into a small saucepan filled with salted water and two dried bay leaves.
Simmer the tentacle over medium heat for thirty minutes until tender when pierced with a fork.
Remove the octopus from hot liquid and slice it into bite-sized half-inch round pieces.
Peel and devein the wild shrimp completely, patting them dry using paper towels carefully.
Trim the tough outer stems from the fresh fennel bulb and slice the main core very thinly.
Dice the red onion into uniform small squares to ensure even cooking throughout the base sauce.
Slice the entire head of garlic horizontally to expose all internal cloves for smooth roasting.
Drizzle exposed garlic cloves with one teaspoon olive oil and wrap tight in aluminum foil.
Roast the wrapped garlic in a preheated oven at four hundred degrees for exactly twenty minutes.
Squeeze the softened garlic cloves out of their skin into a small mixing bowl and mash smoothly.
Heat two tablespoons olive oil in a wide heavy skillet over medium-high flame until shimmering.
Add chopped red onion and sliced fennel bulb to the skillet with a pinch of fine salt.
Sauté the vegetable mixture for six minutes until edges begin to soften and lightly brown.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed red pepper, and dried oregano to coat the cooked vegetables.
Pour in dry white wine to deglaze the skillet surface, scraping up all browned savory bits.
Add whole cherry tomatoes to the pan and allow them to burst slightly under gentle pressure.
Transfer sliced octopus and prepared wild shrimp into the skillet, stirring once to combine.
Cook seafood mixture for three minutes until shrimp turn pink and opaque throughout their center.
Splash red wine vinegar over cooked seafood and turn off the heat under the wide skillet.
Fold in capers and pitted kalamata olives gently to avoid breaking up the soft burst tomatoes.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid to retain moisture while preparing the orzo noodle base.
Bring two cups of vegetable broth and a cup of water to a rolling boil in a deep saucepan.
Add dry orzo pasta into boiling liquid and stir constantly for two minutes to avoid sticking.
Reduce heat to low and cook orzo for nine minutes until pasta reaches perfectly al dente texture.
Drain excess broth from cooked orzo using a fine mesh strainer, reserving two tablespoons liquid.
Return warm orzo to saucepan and stir in mashed roasted garlic along with unsalted butter.
Pour reserved cooking liquid into garlic orzo to form a glossy coating over all pasta grains.
Zest whole fresh lemon directly into saucepan and squeeze in one tablespoon fresh lemon juice.
Toast pine nuts in a clean dry skillet over low heat for three minutes until fragrant and golden.
Chop fresh dill and flat leaf parsley finely using a sharp chef knife on a clean board.
Divide warm roasted garlic orzo evenly between four wide shallow serving bowls using a spoon.
Spoon warm cooked seafood and vegetable mixture evenly over the center of each noodle bowl.
Crumble barrel-aged feta cheese evenly over warm seafood toppings in all four prepared bowls.
Sprinkle toasted pine nuts across top layer of each bowl to add warm roasted nutty crunch.
Garnish every portion generously with minced fresh dill and chopped green flat leaf parsley.
Season each bowl with freshly ground black pepper and a final dash of extra virgin olive oil.
Slice remaining lemon into thin wedges and place one wedge on the edge of each serving bowl.
Check seasoning of sauce and add a light sprinkle of coarse sea salt if extra salt is desired.
Toss bowl contents gently right before eating to blend warm garlic pasta with warm seafood sauce.
Verify temperature of bowl components to ensure dish is served warm immediately after assembly.
Arrange garnishes neatly so colors of green herbs and red tomatoes show clearly on top.
Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges on the side for squeezing fresh over seafood.
